items.title: Notion Calendar → Desktop
items.text: Open Notion task links from Notion Calendar in Notion Desktop rather than opening another browser tab. Both calendar.notion.com and calendar.notion.so are supported.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Install Git and Python 3 first, then clone from GitHub:

mkdir -p ~/Documents/github_repositories
cd ~/Documents/github_repositories
git clone https://github.com/iop098321qwe/notion_calendar_desktop_bridge.git
cd notion_calendar_desktop_bridge
git switch develop
python3 install.py

Until a release is cut, use develop, where the extension source lives. Private repository access requires GitHub authentication. The installer copies files to ~/.local/share/notion-calendar-desktop-bridge; XDG_DATA_HOME overrides the data directory. Keep the checkout separate from that installation directory. No administrator privileges are needed.

Requires a Chromium-based browser supporting MAIN-world content scripts (Chromium 111 or newer), plus Notion Desktop registered for notion:// URLs.

  1. Open brave://extensions (or chrome://extensions).
  2. Enable Developer mode and choose Load unpacked.
  3. Select the installed directory printed by python3 install.py.
  4. Reload Notion Calendar and click a linked Notion task.
  5. Approve the browser's external-application prompt when requested.

To check the desktop protocol handler on Linux:

xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/notion

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• extension/direct.js intercepts Calendar task clicks at document start, during the original user gesture, and hands off in the existing tab.
  • extension/links.mjs validates supported HTTPS Notion task URLs and converts their page IDs into desktop URLs.
  • extension/background.mjs handles otherwise unhandled Calendar navigations.
  • extension/launch.html and launch.mjs provide desktop-launch and explicit web-fallback links when the direct route cannot be used.

The worker remembers source tab IDs in session storage across suspension, not task URLs. Independently opened Notion tabs are left unchanged. The extension uses only the scoped Notion hosts declared in its manifest.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
Requires Node.js with the built-in test runner and Python 3; no npm dependencies are needed to execute the tests.

npm test

The suite covers URL validation, direct handoff, user activation, converter parity, source-tab scoping, navigation races, worker restart, and fallback. Browser APIs are mocked; authenticated Calendar behavior and desktop protocol prompts still need a manual browser check.

items.title: Update and troubleshoot
items.text:
Run these commands from your GitHub checkout:

cd ~/Documents/github_repositories/notion_calendar_desktop_bridge
git switch develop
git pull --ff-only origin develop
python3 install.py

Then open brave://extensions (or chrome://extensions), click Reload on Notion Calendar → Desktop, approve any requested permissions, and reload Calendar. If Brave Origin loads it through launch flags, fully exit all Brave Origin windows, including web apps, and reopen instead. Unpacked extensions do not update automatically from GitHub. If handoff is blocked, use the launch page's desktop button and check the OS protocol handler. Remove the extension in browser settings to uninstall.

items.title: Repository maintenance
items.text:
This repository maintains the extension previously stored in Chezmoi at dot_local/share/notion-calendar-desktop-bridge. The manifest version is unchanged; releases are cut manually.

Chezmoi no longer installs or updates this extension. The repository installer retains the old installed path, so existing browser loading flags still work. Do not load the checkout's extension/ directory as a second copy: its unpacked extension ID may differ. Existing installs only need the update steps.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: This file guides AI coding agents working in notion_calendar_desktop_bridge. All work must follow best practices and industry standards where applicable.

items.title: Scope
items.text: This file covers repository-wide expectations for code, docs, and git work. It does not replace verified instructions in source files, tooling configs, or release automation.

items.title: Formatting Rules
items.text:
• Keep lines at 80 characters or fewer when practical.
  • Allow longer lines only for URLs, code blocks, hashes, or commands that cannot be wrapped cleanly.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text:
• Read README.md first for project context and setup notes.
  • Run git status --short --branch before editing to confirm repo state.
  • Run git diff --stat before committing to review the change scope.
  • Load extension/ unpacked in a Chromium 111+ browser.
  • Run npm test for the Node test suite.

items.title: Environment
items.text:
• Git is required for day-to-day work in this repository.
  • Node.js with node:test is required for tests.
  • Python 3 is required for installation and installer tests.
  • A registered notion:// desktop handler is required for live handoff.
  • No required environment variables are defined.

items.title: Repository Overview
items.text:
• extension/ holds the browser extension.
  • tests/ holds isolated Node browser simulations.
  • docs/ links root documentation; site/ is generated docs output.
  • Root files hold repository tooling and documentation.

items.title: Tracked Files Overview
items.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml: Zensical Pages build and deployment.
  • .gitignore: local dependency and cache exclusions.
  • .husky/commit-msg: commitlint hook.
  • AGENTS.md: repository instructions.
  • LICENSE: repository license.
  • README.md: installation and maintenance guide.
  • commitlint.config.cjs: Conventional Commit validation.
  • docs/AGENTS.md, docs/README.md: root documentation symlinks.
  • done.txt: bootstrap completed-task placeholder.
  • extension/background.mjs: fallback navigation worker.
  • extension/direct.js: user-gesture desktop handoff.
  • extension/launch.html: desktop and web fallback page.
  • extension/launch.mjs: launch-page behavior.
  • extension/links.mjs: validated URL conversion.
  • extension/manifest.json: MV3 permissions and entry points.
  • inbox.txt.tuxedo-lock: bootstrap inbox lock placeholder.
  • install.py: copies extension files to the stable XDG data path.
  • package-lock.json: npm dependency lock.
  • package.json: metadata, test command, and commitlint dependencies.
  • site/: generated documentation; contents omitted from per-file listing.
  • tests/notion-calendar-desktop-bridge.cjs: mocked browser regression suite.
  • tests/test_install.py: isolated installation and update checks.
  • todo.txt: user-only task file; agents must not touch it.
  • zensical.toml: documentation site configuration.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
• A MAIN-world handler intercepts Calendar clicks during user activation.
  • The worker backs up direct handoff with a launch page and web fallback.
  • Keep direct.js and links.mjs URL conversion behavior aligned.
  • Session storage retains source tab IDs, not task URLs.

items.title: Commands
items.text:
• git status --short --branch: show the current branch and worktree state.
  • git diff --stat: review the size and spread of pending changes.
  • git log --oneline --decorate -5: inspect recent commit history.
  • npm test: run isolated regression tests.
  • zensical build --clean: build documentation when installed.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
• npm test covers URL validation, activation, races, and fallback.
  • Confirm live Calendar and desktop protocol prompts manually.
  • Do not claim coverage, test gates, or suites that are not verified.

items.title: Linting and Formatting
items.text:
• Commitlint validates messages through the Husky commit hook.
  • No source formatter is configured.
  • Keep changes minimal and consistent with the existing code style.

items.title: CI and Release
items.text:
• .github/workflows/docs.yml builds Zensical on main and master.
  • Releases are manual; release-note filters are not defined here.
  • Use Conventional Commits for every commit. Prefer a scope when it adds clarity.
  • Never create, edit, or update CHANGELOG.md manually.
  • CHANGELOG.md is generated and maintained by release tooling only.
  • If release automation adds or changes generated files, let the tooling own those updates.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Use small, correct changes that fit the existing project structure.
  • Agents must never read, create, edit, delete, move, stage, commit, or otherwise touch todo.txt; only the user may modify it manually.
  • Prefer amending small related corrections into the relevant unshared current-branch commit instead of separate fixup or cleanup commits.
  • Use standalone, changelog-ready Conventional Commit headers.
  • Verify behavior from the actual codebase before documenting or changing it.
  • Keep AGENTS.md as instructions, not as a changelog, diary, or work log.
  • Do not add update notes, status logs, or change summaries to AGENTS.md.

items.title: Security and Compliance
items.text:
• Never commit secrets, credentials, tokens, or private keys.
  • Verify new dependencies, automation, and scripts before trusting them.

items.title: Dependencies and Services
items.text:
• Notion Calendar and Notion Desktop provide the live integration.
  • No background service, server, or database is installed.
  • Releases are manual; do not change versions as part of migration.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• If repo behavior is unclear, inspect tracked files and git history before making assumptions.
  • If a generated or managed file changes unexpectedly, verify which tool owns it before editing.

items.title: Refining Existing AGENTS.md
items.text:
• Re-check every statement against the repository before keeping it.
  • Remove stale, duplicated, or vague guidance.
  • Replace placeholders with exact commands, paths, and verified workflows.
  • Keep bullets short and easy for AI agents to scan.
  • Preserve this section order when improving the file.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text:
• After any code, config, or doc change, verify that AGENTS.md still matches the repository.
  • When AGENTS.md needs an update, make it in a separate docs Conventional Commit such as docs(agents): update repo instructions.
  • Keep AGENTS.md out of mixed code commits whenever possible.
  • Remove stale instructions instead of appending historical notes.
